curated.model: omr/42081-1 Volvo Concept Wheel Loader ZEUX.mpd
curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42081-1-1.pdf (one book, 260 pages: the loader is steps 1-394 on pages 3-240, the drone pages 241-243; pages 245-249 show each function with green arrows, and pages 250-251 are a two-page overview of all five)

functions.does: The knob on top, between the lift arm and the rear body, steers all four wheels: a shaft down through the chassis turns a pinion on the front steering rack, and a second shaft with universal joints runs back to a pinion on the rear rack, so the front and rear wheels steer opposite ways and the loader turns tightly.
functions.source: book: page 246 (arrows on the top knob and on the front and rear wheels), page 251 (top view with all four wheels steered, front and rear opposite); page 82 shows the rear axle's two steered positions

functions.does: Either of the middle pair of knobs low on the chassis sides, just behind the front wheels, raises and lowers the loader arm: the knob turns the screw of a linear actuator lying along the chassis, which pushes the arm up about its pivot, carrying the bucket with it.
functions.source: book: page 248 (arrow on the knob and an up arrow on the arm), page 250 (the arm in three positions); arm actuator steps on pages 100-106 and 119-120

functions.does: Either of the upper pair of knobs, high on the sides by the arm's pivot, tilts the bucket: a shaft with universal joints runs up the arm to a second linear actuator, which works the bucket through a pair of links at the arm's tip.
functions.source: book: page 247 (arrow on the upper knob and a curved arrow on the bucket), page 250 (the bucket tipped); bucket actuator steps on pages 100-112

functions.does: Either of the lowest pair of knobs, under the chassis sides just behind the front wheels, raises and lowers the back of the loader: a linear actuator lying under the chassis swings the arms that carry the rear axle, so the rear end rises or sinks over the rear wheels.
functions.source: book: page 249 (arrow on the low knob and an up-and-down arrow between the rear body and the rear wheels), page 251 (the back of the loader tilting up); rear actuator steps on pages 50-51; inferred: that it works by swinging the rear axle's arms

functions.does: The knob at the very back slides the whole rear body (the battery pack with the drone pad on top) fore and aft as a counterweight: it turns a worm gear in the body, which walks along a toothed rack on the chassis.
functions.source: book: page 245 (arrow on the rear knob and a fore-and-aft arrow on the rear body), page 251 (the rear body slid back); rack and worm steps on pages 136-140

functions.does: The four wheels roll freely; there's no drive to them.
functions.source: book: wheels on pages 232-236; inferred: that they only roll

functions.does: The drone's four three-bladed propellers spin, and the drone lifts off its pad on top of the rear body to be played with on its own.
functions.source: book: drone on pages 241-243, shown beside the loader on pages 244-251; inferred: that the propellers spin and the drone comes off
functions.note: the model file parks the drone on top of the rear body

functions.does: The two seven-bladed fans set into the top of the rear body spin.
functions.source: inferred: they're propellers on pins; the book doesn't show them moving

functions.does: The work light on its flexible arm above the rear body can be posed on its ball joints.
functions.source: book: pages 229-231 (the light and its arm); inferred: that it's meant to be posed
functions.skip: ball joints pose only; nothing drives them
